cards.title: IBCC plans fully online attestation from Jan 1, ending office visits and courier submissions
cards.author: APP, News Desk
cards.why: This represents a major development in e-governance and the digitisation of public services, which is a key area for CSS/PMS exams regarding administrative reforms.
cards.summary: The Inter Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC) is launching a fully digital attestation service starting January 1, 2027. Students will be able to apply, process, and download verified documents online without needing physical visits or courier services. The initiative covers 29 examination boards and is expected to benefit up to 500,000 students annually.
key_facts: The fully online attestation service will commence on January 1, 2027.
The system will cover qualifications from 29 examination boards across Pakistan.
Applicants will be able to download and print verified documents directly from the IBCC portal.
The initiative aims to save time and reduce costs for 400,000 to 500,000 students annually.
The project was implemented under the directions of the Federal Secretary for Education and Professional Training.

vocab.meaning: The act of certifying a document as being genuine.
Using technology to perform tasks without human intervention.

text: The Inter Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC) will launch a fully online attestation service on Jan 1, 2027, allowing students to apply for attestation and download their attested documents without visiting an IBCC office or sending documents by courier.

The decision was taken at a meeting of the IBCC Board of Directors chaired by Executive Director Dr Ghulam Ali Mallah. The service will cover qualifications issued by 29 examination boards across Pakistan, as well as eligible qualifications from madressahs.

Under the new online service, applicants will submit their documents through the IBCC portal. Once the commission processes and approves an application, the electronically attested document will be available in the applicant’s account to download and print. The new system will eliminate the need for courier delivery in either direction.

Students needing to submit the same document to several institutions will be able to print multiple copies without paying a separate IBCC attestation fee for each copy. They can use the copies for submissions to universities and, where required for use abroad, to the foreign ministry, subject to its applicable requirements.

Dr Mallah said the commission had developed the system on the directions of Federal Secretary for Education and Professional Training Nadeem Mahbub, after the IBCC Board of Governors took up the automation of the entire attestation process.

He said the commission expected the service to benefit an estimated 400,000 to 500,000 students by cutting travel and courier costs and saving them time spent visiting and waiting at IBCC offices. The shift would also reduce the commission’s workload by eliminating the need to receive, handle and dispatch physical documents.

The IBCC is an umbrella board of 29 educational boards in the country that verifies matric and intermediate certificates and provides equivalence certificates against O/A levels and other foreign qualifications.

In February 2025, the board said it had digitised the process for verification of academic degrees issued by boards of intermediate and secondary education. It said this would ensure the integrity and authenticity of the data as well as streamlining the process, ensuring faster and more efficient attestation.

cards.title: Oman to supply petroleum products, $200m credit facility to PSO under new agreement
cards.author: Khaleeq Kiani
cards.why: It illustrates Pakistan's strategic efforts to maintain energy security amidst geopolitical tensions and economic constraints.
cards.summary: Pakistan and Oman have signed a significant energy agreement to secure petroleum supplies for Pakistan State Oil (PSO). The deal includes a $200 million credit facility to facilitate these purchases. This move aims to diversify Pakistan's energy imports amid ongoing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts: Pakistan and Oman signed a Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) for petroleum products.
The agreement provides a $200 million credit line to Pakistan State Oil (PSO).
The deal aims to diversify energy sources as the Strait of Hormuz faces instability.
A Pakistan-Oman Joint Working Group on Oil and Gas has been established to strengthen bilateral cooperation.

vocab.meaning: A type of loan or financial arrangement that allows a borrower to take out money over time.
To broaden the range of sources or activities.

text: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Oman on Sunday signed an agreement under which the Gulf country’s state-owned OQ Trading would supply petroleum products, as well as a $200 million credit line, to the Pakistan State Oil (PSO).
This could provide Pakistan with a means to strategically diversify its sourcing of petroleum products as the Strait of Hormuz continues to be choked by the US-Iran conflict into its ninth month.

According to an announcement from the Petroleum Division, the agreement between the two state-owned entities was signed during Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik’s visit to Muscat, where he met with Oman’s Minister of Energy and Minerals Eng. Salim Al Aufi.
The two sides discussed opportunities for strengthening bilateral cooperation in the oil, gas and minerals sectors.

During the meeting, both ministers discussed avenues for mutually beneficial cooperation and welcomed the establishment of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Working Group on Oil and Gas. They agreed to make optimal use of this institutional mechanism to further strengthen bilateral engagement and advance cooperation in the energy and mining sector.

Following the meeting, the two ministers witnessed the signing of a Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) for petroleum products between PSO and OQ Trading (OQT), Oman’s global commodity trading company. OQT has also agreed to extend a $200m credit line to PSO to facilitate petroleum purchases.

Welcoming the agreement, both ministers expressed confidence that its implementation would further strengthen Pakistan-Oman energy ties and support Pakistan’s efforts to enhance energy security through diversification of energy imports.

“The agreement marks an important milestone in the commercial relationship between the two companies and provides a structured arrangement for petroleum product supplies from OQT to PSO, supporting supply reliability amid continued volatility in regional energy markets,” the Petroleum Division’s statement said.

It noted that OQT has already established itself as a major supplier of gasoline to PSO, supplying more than 1m tonnes during 2026. The newly signed agreement builds on this established trading relationship and provides a framework for expanding commercial cooperation, the statement added.
Beyond gasoline, OQT has also strengthened its presence in Pakistan’s liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) market, supplying both state-owned and private sector buyers.

According to the Petroleum Division, OQT’s LPG supplies to Pakistan are expected to exceed 120,000 metric tonnes by the end of 2026, reflecting the company’s continued commitment to meeting market demand and maintaining energy flows amid regional supply disruptions.

The meeting and the signing of the agreement underscore the shared commitment of Pakistan and Oman to expanding bilateral energy cooperation, strengthening commercial partnerships and exploring new investment opportunities across the oil, gas and minerals sectors, the statement added.
Last month, Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi made a two-day visit to Pakistan, meeting its top leadership.

He attended the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC), during which both sides emphasised the importance of promoting exchanges of business delegations from both countries to unlock new opportunities for trade, investment and institutional collaboration.

cards.title: Pakistan to host annual meeting of IAEA nuclear security network from Nov 23-26
cards.author: News Desk
cards.why: This highlights Pakistan's role in global nuclear governance and compliance with international safety standards.
cards.summary: Pakistan is hosting the 15th annual meeting of the International Network for Nuclear Security Training and Support Centres in Islamabad from November 23-26. The event brings together the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and 49 member states. It focuses on strengthening global nuclear security through international cooperation and capacity building.
key_facts: The 15th annual meeting of the NSSC Network is held in Islamabad from Nov 23-26.
Representatives from 49 member states and the IAEA are participating in the event.
Pakistan previously hosted this network's meeting in 2016.
The network aims to strengthen the sustainability of nuclear security globally.

vocab.meaning: The process of developing and strengthening skills and resources.
The ability to be maintained at a certain level over the long term.

text: Pakistan will host the 15th annual meeting of the International Network for Nuclear Security Training and Support Centres (NSSC Network) in Islamabad from Nov 23-26, in collaboration with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), the Foreign Office (FO) said on Sunday.

The network facilitates cooperation among Nuclear Security Training and Support Centres that the IAEA sets up in collaboration with member states to strengthen the sustainability of nuclear security, according to the IAEA website.

The body’s four-day meeting in Pakistan will bring together representatives of the IAEA and 49 member states of the NSSC Network to discuss ways to strengthen nuclear security training and support, promote international cooperation and exchange experience in this field, the FO statement said.
It added that Pakistan previously hosted the NSSC Network annual meeting in 2016, when it was held for the first time outside the IAEA headquarters in Vienna.

“Hosting the meeting in Islamabad reflects Pakistan’s continued commitment and contribution to advancing nuclear security through international cooperation, knowledge sharing and sustainable capacity building,” the statement said.
